questions.question: Name four properties of metals and give an example of an object that uses each property.
questions.expected_answer: Any four, for example: shiny, like a polished pot or jewellery; hard and strong, like a steel hammer or bridge; malleable, like aluminium foil or car bodies; ductile, like copper wire; high melting point, like pots and stoves.

questions.question: Explain the difference between malleable and ductile.
questions.expected_answer: Malleable means a metal can be hammered, pressed or rolled into a new shape, like aluminium foil. Ductile means a metal can be pulled or drawn into long, thin wire, like copper wire.

questions.question: Where do metals come from, and how do we get them out?
questions.expected_answer: Metals come from rocks called ores in the Earth's crust. Miners dig out the ore in underground mines or open pits, and it is crushed and heated in a furnace to separate the metal. This is called smelting.
